name: Uma' Lasan
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Soriente, Antonia 2003, A classification of Kenyah languages in Sarawak and East Kalimantan, PhD thesis (includes Uma' Lasan phonological material); not found online

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian languages (revised edition). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics, ANU (open access, hdl:1885/10191). Chapter 4 'Sound systems', Borneo section, pp. 183-186.
sources.note: p. 186: 'Unlike the Philippines, stress is not phonemic in any language of Borneo. However, unlike much of the AN world, where stress falls predictably on the penult, many of the languages of coastal Sarawak, and some interior languages have final stress in citation forms, but penultimate stress in phrasal context.' p. 183: Lowland Kenyah dialects Long San, Long Sela'an, Long Ikang (= Western Lowland Kenyah [ttw]) are 'languages, which have final stress in citation forms'; p. 186 Highland Kenyah syllabification (l@koq 'bracelet' -> l@k.koq). Kenyah varieties of Sarawak, not Uma' Lasan; second…

sources.citation: Douglas, R. S. 1911. A comparative vocabulary of the Kayan, Kenyah and Kalabit languages. Sarawak Museum Journal 1(1): 75-119; and Ray, Sidney H. 1913. The languages of Borneo. Sarawak Museum Journal 1(4): 1-196 (archive.org scan of SMJ vol. 1).
sources.note: Douglas: Baram Kenyah (Leppu Buau: Leppu Tau, Jingan, Annan, Sawa) wordlist with a Malay-style orthography note only. Ray: Kenyah appears only in source lists and vocabularies; the single word-stress remark in the volume concerns Ngaju dialects, not Kenyah.

sources.citation: Asih, Yuni Utami. 2017. Inventory of Kenyah Lepo Tau segmental sounds. OKARA: Jurnal Bahasa dan Sastra 11(1). doi:10.19105/ojbs.v11i1.1233.
sources.note: Segmental inventory of Lepo' Tau (Kenyah-Mainstream [xkl], Samarinda), not Uma' Lasan. The only 'stress' remarks concern Indonesian (Lapoliwa: schwa 'usually unstressable', p. 6) and general vowel lengthening 'under stress'; no Kenyah stress rule. Useful for its citations: Lees 1965 (SMJ XII, Lepu' Tau sound system), Rufinus 1992 (Lepo' Bakung sound system, BRC), Soriente 2003 pp. 77-82.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2014. Studying linguistic and cultural contact in Borneo: prospects and challenges. Antropologia 1(1): 59-81.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; repeats the 12 Kayan-Kenyah innovations.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2013. Undergoer voice in Borneo: Penan, Punan, Kenyah and Kayan languages. NUSA 54: 175-203 (hdl:10108/71811).
sources.note: Nothing on stress (morphosyntax of Oma Longh and Lebu' Kulit; 'stress' occurs only as a verb).

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2008. The classification of Kenyah languages: a preliminary statement. In W. Khanittanan & P. Sidwell (eds), SEALS XIV vol. 2 (Pacific Linguistics E-7), 49-62. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gives 12 Kayan-Kenyah shared innovations (no. 12 'Lowering of PAN high vowels *i and *u in penultimate syllable', p. 56) and groups Uma' Alim, Uma' Lasan and Oma Longh together as the Pujungan branch (p. 54); no suprasegmental remarks.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Karl Anderbeck (SIL Indonesia). 2007. Change Request 2007-266: [xky] 'Kenyah, Western' renamed 'Uma' Lasan (Upper Pujungan Kenyah)'.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Establishes identity: Uma' Lasan = Upper Pujungan Kenyah with dialects Uma' Baka and Uma' Alim, marginally intelligible with Uma' Lung [ulu]; cites Soriente 2003 thesis, Soriente 2005 conference paper, Soriente 2006 book.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid umal1239 and Wikipedia 'Uma' Lasan language' pages.
sources.note: No phonology; Glottolog lists no descriptive references (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0); the only language-tagged works are Soriente 1997, Soriente 2003, Sellato 2009 (ethnographic), Ray 1913 and the ISO change request.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2006. Mencaleny & Usung Bayung Marang: a collection of Kenyah stories in the Oma Longh and Lebu' Kulit languages. Jakarta: Atma Jaya University Press. xliii+315 pp. ISBN 9789798850677.

sources.note: Text collection with a long linguistic introduction on Oma Longh (Uma' Lung [ulu]), the sister variety of Uma' Lasan in the Upper Pujungan branch (marginally intelligible); the introduction is the most likely accessible place for an explicit stress statement on Pujungan Kenyah phonology.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2003. A classification of Kenyah variants in Sarawak and Kalimantan. PhD thesis, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, Bangi. xvii+400 pp.

sources.note: The only full-length primary description that treats Uma' Lasan (and Uma' Alim) directly; contains phonological description (Asih 2017 cites pp. 77-82) and is the source behind the ISO/Glottolog identity of xky. Most likely place for a stress statement on Upper Pujungan Kenyah.
